lore:
Since birth, the twins had never been allowed to fly freely with their wings.

The second pair of arms growing from their backs resembled ceremonial vessels that displayed the majesty of the Twin Divi. They were always required to maintain a prescribed posture.

As a child, Pollux had been the more protective of their wings. Every day, he groomed them and applied essential oils, keeping the feathers shining like satin.

Whenever they were briefly alone, he secretly flapped his newly flourishing wings. To Castor's astonishment, he could even lift himself unsteadily from the ground and reach toward the embellished dome above.

Compared with Pollux, who could make his wings dance through a variety of agile poses, Castor often felt that his own were as clumsy as two wooden planks.

Each night, after they went to bed, Castor quietly watched Pollux leap and spin in the darkness, imitating flight within the cramped confines of their room.

<Italic:My brother's wings are so beautiful. But as for me, I may never learn to fly,> Castor thought.

It was on the night of their escape that Castor first felt the cool, liberating evening breeze lift his wings.

Pollux, the more skilled flyer, held tightly to his clumsy brother as they laughed joyfully in the sky, tracing arcs of dives and spins like true birds.

Castor turned his head and saw moonlight gilding Pollux's long, powerful wings, casting a dazzling blue-green halo across the feathers.

<Italic:That must be the most beautiful sight in the world. No matter what happens, I will protect Pollux and safeguard those wings.>

Before long, the harsh wilderness left Pollux's wings wounded by beasts.

Heartbroken, Castor gathered the feathers Pollux had shed and tucked them against his chest, silently vowing that such a thing would never happen again.

But he did not know that one solitary feather would later become his most treasured possession—the last relic he would keep of those wings.
